text.p: Electrical engineering group ABB Asea Brown Boveri AG reported a lower 1996 group net profit and said it expected 1997 net income to reach at least the same level as in 1996.
ABB reported 1996 group net income of $1.233 billion compared with $1.315 billion in 1995.

But it said profits improved at all levels and group net income was in fact 16 percent higher in 1996 if a $250 million extraordinary gain from the transfer of ABB's transportation business to the ABB Daimler-Benz joint venture in 1995 were excluded.
Operating earnings totalled $3.026 billion, down from $3.275 billion for 1995.

ABB AG, formerly known as BBC Brown Boveri AG, is a holding company whose main asset is a 50 percent interest in ABB Asea Brown Boveri. The other 50 percent is owned by Sweden's ABB AB, which was formerly known as ASEA AB.
Commenting on the outlook for 1997, ABB said it expected the global market for new power plants to expand in emerging markets but remain at a low level in industrial nations.
"Within this competitive environment, 1997 orders and earnings for the power generation segment are expected to reach at least the 1996 level," ABB said in a statement.
